editorial:
Fresh off a divorce, Fanny is back in her parents' house with a bright blue sofa, unpaid bills, and zero interest in dating. She cleans houses for a living, but her life feels stuck until she meets Anemone, a traveling professional mermaid who makes the impossible look joyful. The movie mixes small-town French charm with silly costumes, family tension, and a real hunger for freedom. You feel Fanny's frustration, but also her spark, as she starts chasing something that is hers alone. It is less about becoming a mermaid and more about learning to swim in your own life.

What stands out is the easy chemistry between Fanny and Anemone, plus the funny, awkward training scenes that never feel too polished. The family scenes can drag a little, and some jokes land softer than others, but the heart keeps you invested. If you like character-driven comedies with a little ache, this is a good pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you can, or rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night. It is also the kind of feel-good movie you might want on 4K Blu-ray for repeat viewings.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Fanny performs her first real mermaid show and freezes when her ex and family show up. Anemone refuses to push her and instead joins her in the water, turning the moment into a shared performance. Fanny finally lets go of the sofa and debts as symbols of her old life, choosing to keep mermaiding on her own terms. The movie ends with her smiling in the sea, free but not alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven comedies with heart.
